rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the six-compound elution window while minimizing the risk of unretained or missing compounds. This scouting run will identify critical pairs and guide subsequent window, slope, and temperature adjustments.

Injection 1 already achieved the maximum CRF, so retain it as the benchmark. Shorten the gradient at unchanged temperature and endpoints to seek a faster fully resolved separation and measure the critical pairs’ sensitivity to gradient slope.

Both runs achieved the maximum CRF, with resolution still comfortably above 1.5 at eight minutes. Test a four-minute gradient to reduce separation time and approach the slope limit of the early critical pair.

The four-minute gradient retains the maximum CRF but leaves little resolution margin for the first pair. Test higher temperature at unchanged slope to determine whether it improves selectivity while further shortening retention; injection 3 remains the fully resolved fallback.

Heating substantially worsened the first pair’s resolution. Test the lowest temperature at the same gradient to establish whether cooling provides enough selectivity margin for a subsequent two-minute gradient.

Cooling improved the critical pair’s resolution to 2.48. Test the minimum gradient duration at this favorable temperature to establish the speed limit before adjusting the organic window if resolution falls below 1.5.

Narrow the gradient by raising the starting organic fraction, which remains below the first peak’s estimated elution fraction of 0.33. The shallower slope may restore the early pair’s resolution while retaining a strong endpoint for rapid elution of the last compound.

Injection 7 achieves maximum CRF with a 2.66-minute last peak. Raise phi0 one grid step to test whether further window narrowing shortens the separation while preserving early-pair resolution; monitor the first peak for loss of retention.

Raise temperature one step to shorten the separation while testing whether the early pair’s resolution margin remains sufficient. Keep phi0 unchanged because the first peak is already close to the unretained region.

Test one higher starting-organic step to determine whether the shallower slope preserves early-pair resolution or initial-solvent compression becomes limiting. Injection 9 remains the fastest demonstrated fully resolved method, already at maximum CRF.

Return phi0 to 0.30 to avoid the early-peak compression observed at 0.35, and test the next temperature step. This brackets the fastest fully resolved temperature at the current gradient, with injection 9 as the fallback.

Reduce the gradient span to recover the early pair’s resolution at 35 C without increasing gradient duration. The last compound will likely elute during the final hold, so this tests whether improved resolution can retain maximum CRF with a short overall separation.

The early pair barely responded to lowering phi1, suggesting initial-solvent compression limits its resolution at phi0 0.30. Lower phi0 to retain that pair longer and test whether the shallower gradient can restore full resolution at 35 C.

Lower phi1 one more step to make the gradient shallower, targeting the small remaining resolution deficit of the first pair. The last peak may move later during the hold, but the previous 2.85-minute elution leaves ample margin below the scoring threshold.

Injection 14 remains borderline because its first pair is flagged below 1.5 despite rounding. Return to the favorable starting fraction and temperature of injection 9, with a slightly shallower gradient to seek additional resolution margin while keeping the separation short.

Test a more robust short method by combining cooler temperature with a lower starting organic fraction to retain the early pair away from the solvent front. The narrowed gradient should provide resolution margin while the strong endpoint keeps the last peak well below 10 minutes.

Raise temperature one step from injection 16 to test whether its resolution margin permits faster elution while keeping the first peak away from the solvent front. This also assesses a neighboring condition around the established maximum-CRF methods.

Combine the favorable starting fraction of injection 8 with a slightly shallower gradient at the same temperature to seek greater early-pair resolution margin. Maximum CRF is already secured; this tests a nearby short-method alternative with more margin than injection 9.

Test whether a lower starting organic fraction can keep the early peaks farther from the solvent front while retaining full resolution with the fastest endpoint. Injection 7 suggests the critical pair may still clear 1.5, with little increase in last-peak time.

Refine the short, fully resolved region by reducing phi1 one step from injection 16 to increase the critical pair’s resolution margin. This should keep the first peak away from the solvent front and the last peak comfortably below 10 minutes, preserving maximum CRF.

Raise temperature one step from injection 20 to shorten retention while using its early-pair resolution margin. The 25 C and 35 C results bracket this condition, making it a promising maximum-CRF alternative with the first peak retained beyond the solvent front.

Raise phi0 one step from injection 21 to shorten retention while testing a neighboring maximum-CRF condition. At this temperature, phi0 0.30 has preserved full resolution with both stronger endpoints, so this shallower gradient is a low-risk refinement.

Test the cooler neighbor of injection 22 to increase early-pair resolution margin while retaining a short separation. Maximum CRF is already achieved, and injection 9 remains the fastest demonstrated fully resolved method.

Refine injection 19 by lowering phi1 one step to improve its borderline early-pair resolution while keeping the first peak well retained. This should provide another short maximum-CRF method; injection 9 remains the fastest fully resolved result.

Use the final injection to test a slightly shallower neighbor of injection 24, seeking more early-pair resolution margin while maintaining maximum CRF. Injection 9 remains the fastest demonstrated fully resolved method, with the last peak at 2.58 minutes.
